svg.text: PART A - store data: replicate byte / half so it lands in the right lane (select = alu_operation_i[2:0])
PART B - byte enables (wb_write_byte_o[3:0]): by width and by address bits [1:0]
PART C - load path: pick the byte / half from the read word, sign- or zero-extend, then write-back result mux
Fig P6 - WB stage: store byte-lane alignment, byte enables, load alignment / sign-extension, result mux
From your 'wb_write_data / wb_write_byte' mux sketch. SB / SH / SW decide how data and the 4 byte enables are placed in the 32-bit word.
(op2 feeds the three replicate blocks - wiring only)
store_en is the select of the 'store gating' mux (and of the byte-enable mux in Part B);
only a real, non-stalled store may drive data/enables.
write enables for SB: one-hot by address [1:0];
SH: low pair if addr[1]=0, high pair if addr[1]=1;
Only loads use the read data; every other instruction writes ex_result.
Squashed instructions (wb_stall_first / second, Fig P1) have reg write-enable forced to 0 here.
